guards.what: Entangled.cs's own docstring is literal: "This Affliction has no logic of its own." It declares NO override of any AfflictionModel member — not even HasExtraCardText — so there is nothing for this unit to diverge on at the AfflictionModel layer; every observable behavior is TangledPower's.
guards.maps_to: `EntangledAffliction` (afflictions.py) is likewise a bare data-only subclass with no method overrides beyond the constructor. Symmetric with the C# split.

TangledPower.AfterApplied (TangledPower.cs:22-28) afflicts every Attack card in the player's hand/piles at power-grant time; AfterCardEnteredCombat (:30-36) afflicts a newly-entering unafflicted Attack card; TryModifyEnergyCostInCombat (:60-67) raises an Entangled Attack's cost by `base.Amount`; AfterSideTurnEnd (:38-44) self-removes the power (Flash + PowerCmd.Remove), whose AfterRemoved (:46-52) sweeps every Entangled affliction off `AllCards`. Mirrored by `power/tangled` (powers.py), already audited: rollup verdict `faithful` — every entry closed. Applier confirmed ported: `sts2_rl/monsters/overgrowth/vine_shambler.py`.

Entangled overrides no `IsStackable`, inheriting AfflictionModel's default `False` (AfflictionModel.cs:127-130); `EntangledAffliction` leaves the base `is_stackable = False` unoverridden the same way.

Entangled is card-scoped to the player's own Attack cards (no monster deck exists, so this is a player-only affliction like all seven). It is a SINGLE-TURN debuff by construction: TangledPower removes ITSELF at AfterSideTurnEnd every side-turn-end the owner participates in, and that removal's AfterRemoved sweep is what actually clears the card markers — so Entangled cannot outlive the turn it (and the power carrying it) was applied on. No AfterDeath override exists on TangledPower; TangledPower is carried by the PLAYER (an enemy-inflicted debuff), so there is no applier-death removal path to check, the same shape as Bound's ChainsOfBindingPower.
